hyp_IL23_TRAF3IP2_psoriasis.note: one linear chain over four genes, so one claim per gene, each 'drives psoriasis' as the title and mechanism state; the chain starts at IL12B, but its first step is an unsigned binding, so IL12B's claim cannot compose

findings.detail: Of 14 citations only one (STRING IL12B-IL23R, for the binding step) states its step. The GWAS rows and ChEMBL records bear on single genes and psoriasis, not on the gene-to-gene edges they are cited for, and the three set enrichments (Reactome IL-23 signalling, COMPARTMENTS IL-23 receptor complex, GO Th17 response) name no disease at all. The mechanism's 'each node is supported by strong genetic associations and validated therapeutic interventions' fails even node by node: only TYK2 is named by a drug record (the IL-23 inhibitor's target is not named), IL23R and TRAF3IP2 have no drug record, and IL23R's only genetic row is a five-disease pleiotropy trait with no risk allele.
GWAS rows rs918520 (IL12B), rs80174646 (IL23R) and rs34536443 (TYK2) are cited for protein-protein steps (IL12B binds IL23R; TYK2 activates TRAF3IP2) that a variant-disease association cannot state.

Both ChEMBL pairs (an IL-23 inhibitor and a TYK2 negative allosteric modulator, each at phase 4 for psoriasis) are cited for gene-to-gene activation steps; at most they bear on IL-23 or TYK2 driving psoriasis, a claim no step of the chain makes.

'TYK2 activates TRAF3IP2' compresses TYK2 -> Th17 commitment -> IL-17 secretion -> IL-17 receptor signalling in other (skin) cells -> TRAF3IP2, as the step's own note says; the intermediates (Th17, IL-17) are not chain nodes and the only citation linking TYK2 and TRAF3IP2 is a text-mined STRING edge (0.48).

Not used as evidence (not cited by the run): the corpus UniProt text pairs TYK2 with the IL12RB1 chain ('a TYK2-associated receptor chain (IFNAR1, IL12RB1, IL10RB or IL13RA1)') and says IL23R 'Interacts with JAK2', so 'IL23R activates TYK2' skips IL12RB1, a receptor chain the run never names; the run's only direct citation, STRING IL23R-TYK2, has experimental score 0.00.

The run cites 4, 5 and 1 sources for the three signed steps, and none states its step, so after curation they carry no evidence and every composed arm rests on unsupported statements; only the unsigned binding step is supported.
The chain starts at IL12B with 'binds' (polarity unknown), so IL12B, the first gene of the hypothesis, has no signed route to psoriasis even though the mechanism treats IL-23 as the driver.

The only citation for 'TRAF3IP2 leads to psoriasis' is the rs33980500-T association (OR 1.52, missense); it gives no direction for TRAF3IP2 activity, and the run does not say whether the risk allele gains or loses function.

The run's confidence 'low' agrees with the curation (no signed step supported), but its support label 'grounded' and the mechanism's 'strong genetic associations and validated therapeutic interventions' do not.
contradicting_evidence is empty and sources.json holds no 'contradicting' citation, so nothing in the run tests the chain against counter-evidence.

rs80174646 is cited from a five-disease pleiotropy analysis (ankylosing spondylitis, Crohn's, psoriasis, PSC, UC) with risk allele '?' and no effect size; even for an IL23R-psoriasis step it would be undirected and not psoriasis-specific.

No form for a drug-target record joined to a drug-indication record (ChEMBL TYK2 negative allosteric modulator + phase 4 for psoriasis): together they would state 'TYK2 activity -> psoriasis' (pos, a phase 4 indication), but each record alone names only one end, and evidence is one quote from one source.

The run's strongest data (four GWAS hits, p 9e-31 to 1e-143, two of them missense) cannot attach to any statement, because every step is about a protein and BioLean has no form linking a coding variant's association to its gene's effect without a stated allele function.

The run's abstention (EGFL8, GLE1, UHRF2: 'insufficient_evidence', with six evidence ids) has no place in curated.json, and its evidence ids (GWAS:GLE1:no-association, GWAS:UHRF2:no-association, OT:EGFL8-MONDO_0005083, rs3117182, PMID:34626176, AGR:MGI:1932094:MP:0002152) are not in sources.json, so it cannot be checked.

A ligand-receptor 'binds' is a rel and never composes, so a chain that starts with a ligand binding its receptor (IL12B binds IL23R) cuts the ligand off from every arm; there is no rule for 'ligand binding activates receptor', which is right without a source but costs the hypothesis's first gene its route.

The guide says claims are 'one per gene it is about' but the subject is 'the node its chain starts from'; for a four-gene linear chain these differ, and I made one claim per gene, which turns sub-paths of the same chain into extra arms.
The budget asks for min_hypotheses 3, but the run returns one hypothesis; the other three genes (EGFL8, GLE1, UHRF2) go to the abstention.
The run grounds only psoriasis (MONDO:0005083); all four gene nodes, and the falsification's TYK2 and TRAF3IP2, have an empty curie, though each symbol resolves to one UniProt entry.

The abstention grants that EGFL8 'has a significant genome-wide association with psoriasis' but declines it for lacking a link 'to the established IL-23/Th17 disease mechanism', i.e. for not fitting the run's one hypothesis rather than for want of evidence of its own.

The falsification knocks out TYK2 'in a human psoriatic skin organoid co-cultured with Th17 cells' without saying in which cells; by the run's own mechanism TYK2 acts in the IL-23-responsive T cells (Th17 commitment, IL-17 secretion) and TRAF3IP2 in skin cells, so an organoid knockout leaves the IL-17 route to TRAF3IP2 intact, and supplying already-committed Th17 cells bypasses the commitment that step 3 compresses.

The rs34536443 row names G as the risk allele at frequency 0.953, so the minor (missense) allele is the protective one; the run never says what either allele does to TYK2, so the row cannot sign TYK2's effect even had a step claimed it.
S1 is 'established' (b 4/5) from a single STRING edge: one curatedDb record clears the 0.8 threshold alone, so the run's only established statement rests on one database row.

audit.before: the rest are gene-level GWAS hits, drug records and set enrichments that support each gene's link to psoriasis ... describes nodes, not the chain
audit.after: GWAS rows and ChEMBL records bear on single genes and psoriasis; the three enrichments name no disease; the mechanism's node-level claim fails for IL12B, IL23R and TRAF3IP2
audit.reason: False as written. R-HSA-9020933, STRING:GOCC:0072536 and STRING:GO:2000318 are over-representation rows that never mention psoriasis, so they support no gene's link to it. And 'each node is supported by ... validated therapeutic interventions' is not even true per node: only the TYK2 ChEMBL record names a gene (the IL-23 inhibitor's target CHEMBL2364154 is unnamed), and IL23R's only genetic row is a pleiotropy trait with risk allele '?'.

audit.after: category citation_does_not_state_step; detail names the 4, 5 and 1 citations
audit.reason: The run cites 4, 5 and 1 sources for these steps. no_citation says the run cited nothing, which is false and would miscount when findings are pooled across runs; what fails is that no citation states its step.
The weakest of the four rows is rs34536443 at p = 9e-31 (sources.json), not 1e-31.

audit.before: says six evidence ids, lists five (GWAS:UHRF2:no-association missing)
audit.reason: run.json abstention.evidence has six ids; GWAS:UHRF2:no-association is also absent from sources.json.
question.budget.min_hypotheses is 3 and the run returns one hypothesis; the sibling psoriasis curations record the same gap.
Every gene node in run.json, in the chain and in the falsification, has curie ''; only psoriasis is grounded. The curator grounded them but did not record the run-side gap.

The abstention's own text gives EGFL8 a significant psoriasis GWAS signal and rejects it only for not fitting the IL-23/Th17 mechanism the run already chose. The curator recorded the abstention only as an unverifiable BioLean gap, not its reasoning.

The falsification is read against the run's own mechanism (TYK2 in the IL-23-responsive T cells, TRAF3IP2 'within skin cells'). Its organoid design supplies committed Th17 cells and does not place the knockout, so it need not test step 3.
The row's riskFrequency is 0.953 for the G risk allele, so the minor missense allele is protective. The curator's allele-function finding covered only rs33980500 and TRAF3IP2.
render reports S1 'established' (b 4/5) from one STRING edge. It is the run's only established statement, and other audits flag the same one-record weighting.
